prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No open or discoverable AI reliably designs any molecule with a requested property; open tools generate property-scored candidates whose properties are predicted, not met. REINVENT 4 (Apache 2.0) does reinforcement-learning inverse design for small molecules (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/pmid/38383444). Reviews in 2025 to 2026 name limited synthesizability and property-prediction accuracy as the unsolved gap (https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlepdf/2026/sc/d5sc05225d, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12323263), and reported inverse-design success rates are computational, e.g. 7.1 to 38.9 percent first-principles-validated for crystals (https://oar.a-star.edu.sg/communities-collections/articles/18130). Enumerated make-on-demand space already exceeds 83 billion molecules but is reaction-rule enumeration, not property design (https://www.biosolveit.de/2025/09/23/enamines-real-space-september-2025-update-now-83-billion/). Honest limit: the KPI count of 1,000,000,000 molecules designed is trivially reachable by raw generation with existing open tools, so it is only meaningful if counted as molecules whose requested property is confirmed; generation-only tasks are known answers and need their own prior-art basis.
